title: China and Japan fill the U19 mixed doubles semi-finals at the World Youth Championships as India's top seeds fall
seo_title: World Youth Championships: China and Japan in mixed semis
description: Japan's Nakano and Takahashi beat India's top seeds as China and Japan took all four U19 mixed doubles medal places at the World Youth Championships.
standfirst: Mao Takamori and Aoba Takahashi also reached the girls' doubles semi-finals, and France's Leana Hochart and Antoine Noirault recovered from a mixed doubles defeat to secure medals in Istanbul.

sides.name: Su Tsz Tung / Mak Ming Shum

body: China and Japan will share the four U19 mixed doubles medals at the World Youth Championships in Istanbul after Japan's Kohaku Nakano and Aoba Takahashi beat India's top seeds, Abhinandh Pradhivadhi and Divyanshi Bhowmick, 11-5, 12-10, 11-8 in the quarter-finals on Tuesday.

Semi-final losers take bronze, so all four pairs left are medallists. The semi-finals were due to start at about 5pm UK time, with Nakano and Takahashi against China's Wen Ruibo and Jiang Yiyi, and Japan's Shunto Iwaida and Mao Takamori against the second seeds, Li Hechen and Yao Ruixuan. The final is on Thursday at about 5pm UK time.
## Iwaida and Takamori come through a decider

The closest of the mixed quarter-finals was also the strangest start. France's Antoine Noirault and Leana Hochart won the first game 11-2 against Iwaida and Takamori, who then had to come from 2-1 down. They took the fourth 11-8 and the decider 11-9 after 39 minutes. It was their second notable win in two days: on Monday they [won a game 11-0](/news/world-youth-championships-2026-u19-mixed-doubles-last-16-iwaida-takamori-arpas-berzosa.html) against the third seeds, Samuel Arpas and Maria Berzosa.

China's pairs were more comfortable. Wen and Jiang, who each won twice in China's [team finals on Monday](/news/world-youth-championships-2026-u19-team-finals-china-beat-taiwan-japan.html), lost the first game 11-9 to Poland's Patryk Zyworonek and Germany's Koharu Itagaki, then won the next three, the last two 11-4, 11-5. Li and Yao beat South Korea's Lee Hyeonho and Heo Yerim 11-9, 11-5, 11-8 in 22 minutes.

The U19 doubles quarter-finals followed, and several of the same players secured a second medal. In the girls' event Takamori and Takahashi beat Taiwan's Wu Ying Syuan and Wu Jia-En 11-8, 13-11, 7-11, 13-11, and China's second seeds, Jiang and Yao, came from a game down to beat Russia's Zlata Terekhova and Eseniia Shirokova 5-11, 13-11, 11-4, 12-10.

Hochart recovered from her mixed doubles defeat to reach the semi-finals with Alexia Nodin. The French fourth seeds beat Hong Kong's sixth seeds, Su Tsz Tung and Mak Ming Shum, 11-9 in the fifth game of a 44-minute match. South Korea's top seeds, Jeong Yein and Heo Yerim, beat the Americans Sally Moyland and Lilian Ma 11-8, 11-7, 9-11, 11-3.

In the boys' doubles the top seeds, Wen and Li, beat Iwaida and Nakano 11-9, 11-6, 11-4 in 21 minutes. Noirault also has a medal: he and Nathan Pilard, the fourth seeds, beat Enrique Rios of Puerto Rico and Ramon Vila of the Dominican Republic 11-6 in the fifth game. They play Wen and Li in the semi-finals. In the other two quarter-finals Kazakhstan's Alan Kurmangaliyev and Iran's Benyamin Faraji, the third seeds, beat India's sixth seeds 18-16 in the fourth game and 11-9 in the fifth, and South Korea's Kim Daehwan and Lee Hyeonho beat Taiwan's Hung Che-Yen and Lin Chin-Ting in four.

- U19 mixed doubles, quarter-finals: Kohaku Nakano and Aoba Takahashi (JPN) bt Abhinandh Pradhivadhi and Divyanshi Bhowmick (IND) 11-5, 12-10, 11-8; Wen Ruibo and Jiang Yiyi (CHN) bt Patryk Zyworonek and Koharu Itagaki (POL/GER) 9-11, 12-10, 11-4, 11-5; Shunto Iwaida and Mao Takamori (JPN) bt Antoine Noirault and Leana Hochart (FRA) 2-11, 11-8, 10-12, 11-8, 11-9; Li Hechen and Yao Ruixuan (CHN) bt Lee Hyeonho and Heo Yerim (KOR) 11-9, 11-5, 11-8
- U19 girls' doubles, quarter-finals: Jeong Yein and Heo Yerim (KOR) bt Sally Moyland and Lilian Ma (USA) 11-8, 11-7, 9-11, 11-3; Leana Hochart and Alexia Nodin (FRA) bt Su Tsz Tung and Mak Ming Shum (HKG) 11-9, 8-11, 11-9, 9-11, 11-9; Mao Takamori and Aoba Takahashi (JPN) bt Wu Ying Syuan and Wu Jia-En (TPE) 11-8, 13-11, 7-11, 13-11; Jiang Yiyi and Yao Ruixuan (CHN) bt Zlata Terekhova and Eseniia Shirokova (RUS) 5-11, 13-11, 11-4, 12-10
- U19 boys' doubles, quarter-finals: Wen Ruibo and Li Hechen (CHN) bt Shunto Iwaida and Kohaku Nakano (JPN) 11-9, 11-6, 11-4; Nathan Pilard and Antoine Noirault (FRA) bt Enrique Rios and Ramon Vila (PUR/DOM) 11-6, 10-12, 11-7, 9-11, 11-6; Alan Kurmangaliyev and Benyamin Faraji (KAZ/IRI) bt Abhinandh Pradhivadhi and Priyanuj Bhattacharyya (IND) 11-9, 8-11, 7-11, 18-16, 11-9; Kim Daehwan and Lee Hyeonho (KOR) bt Hung Che-Yen and Lin Chin-Ting (TPE) 13-11, 11-9, 9-11, 12-10

The U19 singles start on Wednesday, with the last 32 from midday UK time. The doubles semi-finals are on Thursday from about 2.30pm UK time: Jeong and Heo play Hochart and Nodin, and Takamori and Takahashi play Jiang and Yao, with Wen and Li against Pilard and Noirault, and Kurmangaliyev and Faraji against Kim and Lee, in the boys' draw. Times are approximate; live scores and the draws are on Eleven's [event page](/events/world-youth-championships-2026.html).
